51263493.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to CypD (unknown origin) assessed as dissociation constant by SPR analysis

original_paragraph.SPR binding assay: Fragment screening by SPR was run on a Biacore4000 instrument (Biacore AB, GE Healthcare Life Sciences, Uppsala, Sweden). Four Cyclophilin D surfaces of different protein densities with one reference spot have been used. Recombinant human Cyclophilin D protein (amino acids 44-207, K175I) expressed on E. coli was covalently immobilized via standard amine coupling on a CM7 chip at 25°C to immobilization levels between 4,000 to 12,000 response units. The immobilization buffer contained 20 mM HEPES/NaOH (pH 7.4), 150 mM NaCl, 0.3 mM DTT, 0.1 mM EDTA, 0.05% Tween 20. The published Cyclophilin D inhibitor 2 was used as a control. Each fragment was tested in the primary screen at a single concentration of 2000 µM. The following criteria were defined to assign primary fragment hits: (1) response signals range between 5 to 90 RU per 100 Da MW of the fragment, (2) expected fragment binding levels in agreement with different surface densities of the target protein, (3) level of binding signal suppressed by at least 50% in competition set-up with 200 nM CsA for at least 3 protein surfaces/spots. Inhibitors (stored as 10 mM stock solutions in 100% DMSO) or fragments (stored as 100 mM stock solutions in 100% DMSO) were diluted in running buffer (20 mM HEPES/NaOH pH 7.4, 150 mM NaCl, 0.3 mM DTT, 0.1 mM EDTA, 0.05% Tween 20, 2% DMSO @25°C) and analysed with a Biacore 4000 or Biacore S51 (Biacore AB, GE Healthcare Life Sciences, Uppsala, Sweden) using a 2-fold dilution series of 10 steps. Interaction analysis cycles were run at 30 /min and consisted of a 180 s sample injection followed by 240 s of buffer flow (dissociation phase). All sensograms were evaluated by first subtracting the binding response recorded from the control surface (reference spot), followed by subtracting a buffer blank injection. To determine kinetic rate constants, data sets were fitted to a simple 1:1 interaction model including a term for mass transport using numerical integration and nonlinear curve fitting. Equilibrium analysis was performed by fitting the response at the end of the association phase to a single-site binding isotherm.
